subtallies.name: On the card's wording
cells: Square (CatalogCategoryType: REGULAR / MENU / KITCHEN — function, not folder/type)
(c) one kind + a switch that lets the rule tighten
Akeneo (only_leaves — per TREE, not per node)
Amazon (type and tree are different objects)
Tokopedia Era B (permission_statuses gates who may list)
Salesforce B2C (roles per assignment, not kinds per node)

framing: Twelve of thirteen ship one kind of node. The card's option (c) names Akeneo — and Akeneo's only_leaves is a per-tree setting, so the correction is one of scope, not existence: “one precedent of thirteen at tree scope; none at node scope.” eBay, Shopee, Tokopedia B enforce leaf-only but leafness there is derived from structure (B2's question, not B1's). Nothing to quote for the absence of a node-kind discriminator — absence of a feature is rarely explained.

rows.h: two objects, one kind of node in each
rows.shape: The attribute owner is ProductType, published required: ["marketplaceIds","name","displayName"], “no parent, ProductTypeList a flat array”; the browse tree (BrowseNode, 598,957 ids across 24 locales) is a separate object.

TaxonomyCategory, 11 fields whole, incl. isRoot Boolean!, isLeaf Boolean!, isArchived Boolean! — three derived flags on one type. Inference: the taxonomy is authored centrally by Shopify; a node kind would be a governance affordance for authors who do not exist on the merchant side.
“every line is id - path” — there is no node object at all (5,595 nodes, depth 7, in a text file).

rows.h: leaf-only enforced (error 62009) but leafness is derived from structure
rows.shape: One node type; leafCategoryTreeNode “true on 15,111 nodes and absent on the other 1,994”, childCategoryTreeNodes present on exactly those 1,994. Inference: every per-category policy (item conditions, aspects, parts compatibility, negotiated price, identifier policy) is keyed on the leaf id — a second kind of node would need a second policy table.
“6,967 sibling PT keys in one flat map, $ref = 0 across 451,013,258 B”; “no category field in the feed at all” — the taxonomy is a workbook (24 categories, 77 subcategories, 461 type groups).
One tree; “has_children = false means the last level category”; only last-level categories retrieve attributes.

rows.h: Era A (b); Era B ambiguous — permission_statuses is a per-node gate on who may list
rows.shape: Era A: Category {name, id, child []object} (3 of 3 rows). Era B: Category {id, parent_id, local_name: string ("Home Supplies"), is_leaf: bool, permission_statuses: []string} — INVITE_ONLY categories need “a separate application through the Qualification Center.”

rows.h: the only one — and the kinds are function (menu, kitchen), not folder/type
rows.shape: CatalogCategoryType has 3 values: REGULAR_CATEGORY, MENU_CATEGORY, KITCHEN_CATEGORY, on a node that also has is_top_level, parent_category, path_to_root, root_category. Stated consequence, not reason: “When a seller creates their menu through the Square Dashboard, the system automatically creates catalog categories with a CategoryType of MENU_CATEGORY … Filter for categories where CategoryType = REGULAR_CATEGORY.” Inference: two surfaces (till, kitchen display) write into one tree.

rows.h: one kind of node, three roles per assignment
rows.shape: “three roles on one Category type — classification 0..1 (attribute set), primary 0..1 per catalog (breadcrumb), assignments 0..N”; only the classification category owns the attribute set.

Category: attributes absent (grep -c attributes Category.orm.yml = 0). Leaf-only is a per-tree only_leaves setting. Stated obliquely: “A category is a way of classifying products… A product can be classified in one or n categories.” vs “A product can belong to only one family.” — kinds are unnecessary because the schema lives on a different object.
“a product_cat term carries no attribute definitions (9 properties, whole list)”.
The Category tree owns no attribute definitions; ProductType is flat and separate. (The “leaf occurs 0 times in 5,366,096 B of spec” figure answers B2, not B1.)

rows.h: per-node flags exist, but they are not “accepts products”
rows.shape: One category entity, with per-node behaviour flags is_anchor / custom_use_parent_settings (display switches); a category carries its own attribute_set_id, unrelated to its products'. Inference: no folder/type kind needed because the product's type (attribute_set_id) is a separate scalar.
